transcript: Last night I saw Marry Me, a new play at New York Theater Workshop, and I don't really know what to make of it. I laughed a lot. I thought it was wildly entertaining, but I feel like I couldn't really figure it out. In very basic terms, I would describe it as queer comedy with explicit references to and subversions of theatrical structures and relationship archetypes. The plot involves an island, the navy, an angel, a psychiatrist. It's really quite absurd in some. I felt like it was a mosaic of many ideas very joyfully and comedically explored, but maybe a bit muddy if you're looking for, like, a single crux or thesis kind of concept. And maybe that's what the playwright intended, but I was a little lost at times. All that said, at 90 minutes with no intermission and the last rolling, I was gladly just along for the ride with that. Another program for my collection.
